points.point: Headline '0.251 USD/kWh' and '85.8 %' renewable share are conditional on diesel-off operation: the reserve case puts the same design at '0.414 USD/kWh' and shrinks the least-cost optimum to '1,500 kWp' PV and '1,000 kWh' battery, so the case is not robust to a must-run diesel requirement.

Operating '7,302 h/yr' with no diesel requires the '19,000 kWh' battery to hold a '1,422 kW' peak island grid, but grid-forming control, frequency/voltage regulation, protection, fault current and black-start capability are not demonstrated.

Annual demand '9,568,110 kWh/yr' with peak '1,422 kW' implies a high 76.8% load factor, while the underlying Hiron source is itself flagged for irreconcilable load/energy statements and an impossible PV yield of '4,291 kWh/kWp'; no reconciled metered PLN load series is shown.
points.addressed_in: The published study we used: Hiron 2021 (Energies 14, 8311)

points.point: The diesel fleet is modelled as '2' x '1,800 kW' although the same source also prints '2 x 2.7 MW'; at min-load '0.25' that changes one-unit minimum output from 450 kW to 675 kW, while diesel capital is treated as sunk, O&M is a flat '0.03 USD/kWh', and fuel-curve coefficients '0.08' and '0.25' are assumed rather than measured.

Fuel price '0.848485 USD/L' is derived from '14000 IDR per liter' in a palm-oil-waste article with FX '16500 IDR per USD assumed', not from a Karimunjawa delivered-diesel or PLN transfer price; this drives the diesel-only comparator '0.354 USD/kWh' and the claimed fuel saving of '3,104,445 L/yr'.

Key costs are transferred without a remote-island delivered-cost build-up: PV capex '1119.0 USD/kWp', PV O&M '24.38 USD/kWp/yr' from a rooftop-mosque study, battery capex '300.0 USD/kWh' assumed, battery O&M '5.0 USD/kWh/yr' assumed, and discount rate '0.08' assumed.

Battery sizing and efficiency are not independently validated: power '4,750 kW' is forced as '19,000 kWh / 4.0 h' and is 3.3 times peak demand '1,422 kW'; gate G2 reports discharge '4,725,626' kWh exactly equal to stored '4,725,626' kWh despite assumed round-trip efficiency '0.9', and battery life is fixed at '12 yr' despite about 4.73 GWh/yr throughput.

Land margin is thin: the main design needs '8.3 ha' of the '9.0 ha' set aside using '0.87 MWdc/ha', leaving little explicit room for battery/inverter areas, access, setbacks and shading, while land ownership and permits remain unresolved.

Reliability is not demonstrated beyond an hourly balance: unserved energy is capped at '0.001' of load, but actual unserved kWh, loss-of-load hours, N-1 diesel or battery outages, sub-hourly cloud ramps and multi-day low-solar events are not reported; the diesel minimum-load margin in G4 is '0.0' kW.

The investor cannot audit net present cost '23,591,478 USD' or LCOE '0.251 USD/kWh' from a cash-flow breakdown: no year-by-year schedule is given for fuel, O&M, battery replacement at '12 yr' within a '20 yr' project, PV life '25 yr', salvage value, diesel overhaul or replacement, taxes or financing.
